formula: The generating  function for partitions whose parts differ by at least 2 with exactly k parts is (famously) q^(k^2)/((1-q)*...*(1-q^k)).

Indeed, if you take any such partition and remove 1 from the smallest part, 3 from the second-smallest part, etc., you remove 1+3+...+(2k-1) = k^2 and are left with an ordinary partition whose number of parts is <= k whose generating function is 1/((1-q)*...*(1-q)^k).

Summing these up famously gives the generating function for partitions whose differences is >= 2. Sticking a (-1)^k in front gives the generating function for the difference between such partitions with an even number of parts and an odd number of parts, since (-1)^even=1 and (-1)^odd=-1. (End)

Applying Maple's ZeilbergerRecurrence command to the above series of Walsh for a(n) results in the first-order recurrence equation (n - 1)*a(n+1) = n*(n + 1)*a(n) - 2^(n+2) with a(0) = 1 and a(2) = 18. Using this it is easy to verify that a(n) satisfies the second-order recurrence a(n) = (n + 3)*a(n-1) - 2*(n - 1)*a(n-2) conjectured above by Mathar.

The sequence b(n) = n!*(n - 1) satisfies the same second-order recurrence but with the initial conditions b(0) = -1 and b(1) = 0. This leads to the finite continued fraction expansion a(n)/b(n) = 9 - 2*( 4/(6 - 6/(7 - 8/(9 - ... - 2*n/(n + 4)))) ) valid for n >= 2. Letting n tend to infinity produces the infinite continued fraction expansion e^2 = 9 - 2*( 4/(6 - 6/(7 - 8/(9 - ... - 2*n/(n + 4 - ...)))) ). (End)

a(n) = 9^n * Gamma(n+2/3) / ((n+1) * Gamma(2/3) * Gamma(n+1)). - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Feb 09 2014
A097188.name: G.f. A(x) satisfies A057083(x*A(x)) = A(x) and so equals the ratio of the g.f.s of any two adjacent diagonals of triangle A097186.

A097189.name: Row sums of triangle A097186, in which the n-th row polynomial R_n(y) is formed from the initial (n+1) terms of g.f. A057083(y)^(n+1), where R_n(1/3) = 3^n for all n >= 0.

A101596.name: Expansion of g.f. c(2*x)^4, where c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.

The positive sequence 1,2,2,0,2,... has g.f. 2(1+x)-sqrt(1-4x^2). - _Paul Barry_, Oct 10 2007

G.f.: 2*S(0) -1-2*x-4*x^2, where S(k) = 2*k+1 + x^2*(2*k+3)/(1 + x^2*(2*k+1)/S(k+1) ); (continued fraction). - _Sergei N. Gladkovskii_, Dec 23 2013
A104624.name: Expansion of exp( arcsinh( -2*x ) ) in powers of x.

A106181.name: Expansion of c(-x^2)(1+2x-sqrt(1+4x^2))/2, c(x) the g.f. of A000108.

For m >= 0 and any constants r, s, define a_{m,r,s}(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} binomial(n+(m-1)*k,m*k) * (r*binomial(n+m*k,k) - s*binomial(n+m*k,k-1)). A_{m,r,s}(x) = Sum_{n>=0} a_{m,r,s}(n)*x^n = t*(1+t^m)*(r+(r+s)*t^(m-1)-s*t^m)/((1+t^(m-1))*(1+(m+1)*t^m-m*t^(m+1))), where t = t(x) satisfies t = 1 + x*t*(1+t^m). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Jun 27 2026
A116363.name: a(n) = dot product of row n in Catalan triangle A033184 with row n in Pascal's triangle.

A116387.name: Expansion of 1/(sqrt(1-2*x-3*x^2)*(2-M(x))), where M(x) is the g.f. of the Motzkin numbers A001006.

A116388.name: Expansion of 1/((1+x*(1-M(x)))*sqrt(1-2*x-3*x^2)), M(x) the g.f. of A001006.

formula: If n = 1, a(n)=1. If 2 <= n <= 3, then a(n)=n. If n>3 then a(n)=a(n-a(n-1)) + a(n-1-a(n-2)) + a(n-2-a(n-3))
a(n) = A007844(n)/3. - _Michel Marcus_, Aug 19 2013, conjectured. This is true: see the analogous sequence A007843 for a sketch of the proof. - _M. F. Hasler_, Dec 27 2019
A120503.name: Generalized meta-Fibonacci sequence a(n) with parameters s=0 and k=3.

formula: G.f. A(x) satisfies: 0 = 1 - A(x) + A(x)^2 * x * c(x) where c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.
a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} A106566(n, k)*A000108(k). - _Philippe Deléham_, Jun 20 2007
a(n) = (Sum_{m=1..n} (m*Sum_{k=m..n} binomial(2*k-m-1, k-1)*binomial(2*n-k-1, n-1)))/n, a(0)=1. - _Vladimir Kruchinin_, Oct 08 2011
G.f.: A(x) = 1 + x*c(x)^2*m(x*c(x)^2), where m(x) is the g.f. of A001006 and c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.
a(n) = Catalan(n - 1) * hypergeom([3/2, 2, 1 - n], [3, 2 - 2*n], 4) for n >= 1.
The G.f. satisfies the algebraic equation 0 = F^4*x - F^3 + 2*F^2 - 2*F + 1. - _F. Chapoton_, Oct 18 2021
A127632.name: Expansion of c(x*c(x)), where c(x) is the g.f. for A000108.

A129147.name: Expansion of c(x(1+2x)), c(x) the g.f. of A000108.

formula: Integral representation: a(n) = (2/Pi)*Integral_{x=0..20} x^n*sqrt(x*(20-x))/(x*(16+x)). - _Paul Barry_, Sep 15 2009
a(n) = upper left term in M^n, M = an infinite square production matrix as follows:
A132864.name: Expansion of 1/(1-4x*c(5x)), where c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.

formula: G.f.: 1/(1-v-v^2) where v=(2/sqrt(3))*sin(arcsin(x*3*sqrt(3)/2)/3) is the series reversion of x(1-x^2). [Corrected by _Paul D. Hanna_, Feb 24 2015]
a(n) = top left term of M^n. a(n+1) = sum of top row terms of M^n. Example: top row of M^3 = (4, 3, 1, 1), where a(3) = 4 and a(4) = 9 = (4 + 3 + 1 + 1). (End)
A138164.name: Row sums of Riordan array (c(-x^2),xc(-x^2)^2)^(-1) where c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.

A139376.name: Expansion of 1/((1-x^2*c(x))(1-x-x^2)) where c(x) is the g.f. of A000108.

formula: Equals the Narayana transform (A001263) of integer squares. - _Gary W. Adamson_, Jul 29 2011
A141222.name: Expansion of -1/(2*x) + (2*x-1)^2/(2*x*(1-4x)^(3/2)).

formula: G.f.: Series_Reversion( F_3(x) ), where F_n(x) is the n-th iteration of x*(1 - x).
a(n) = Sum_{0 = x_0 <= x_1 <= x_2 <= x_3 = n-1} Product_{k=0..2} (x_k + 1) * binomial(2*x_{k+1} - x_k + 1,x_{k+1} - x_k)/(2*x_{k+1} - x_k + 1). - _Seiichi Manyama_, May 25 2026
A158826.name: Third iteration of x*C(x) where C(x) is the Catalan function (A000108).

formula: a(n) ~ n! * ((1-exp(-1))*(log(n) + gamma) + exp(-1)), where gamma is the Euler-Mascheroni constant (A001620). - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Oct 02 2013
A162972.name: Number of cycles in all non-derangement permutations of {1,2,...,n}.

A164733.name: Number of n-digit fixed points under the Kaprekar map A151949.

A164734.name: Number of n-digit cycles of length 2 under the Kaprekar map A151949.

A165027.name: Number of n-digit fixed points under the base-4 Kaprekar map A165012.

A165064.name: Number of cycles of n-digit numbers (including fixed points) under the base-6 Kaprekar map A165051.

A165066.name: Number of n-digit fixed points under the base-6 Kaprekar map A165051.

A165125.name: Number of n-digit fixed points under the base-9 Kaprekar map A165110.

formula: G.f.: A(x) = (1/x)*Series_Reversion(x/G(x)^2) where G(x) = g.f. of A004304, where A004304(n) is the number of planar tree-rooted maps with n edges.
G.f.: A(x) = G(x*A(x))^2 where A(x/G(x)^2) = G(x)^2 where G(x) = g.f. of A004304.
a(n) ~ c * 16^n / n^3, where c = 3.07968404... . - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Sep 12 2014
A168452.name: Self-convolution of A005568, where A005568(n) is the product of two successive Catalan numbers C(n)*C(n+1).

formula: a(n) = Sum_{j=0..n} (-1)^j * binomial(2*n+k-j, n-j), with k=6.
A172063.name: Expansion of (2/(3*sqrt(1-4*z)-1+4*z))*((1-sqrt(1-4*z))/(2*z))^k with k=6.

formula: a(n) = Sum_{j=0..n} (-1)^j * binomial(2*n+k-j, n-j), with k=7.
A172064.name: Expansion of (2/(3*sqrt(1-4*z)-1+4*z))*((1-sqrt(1-4*z))/(2*z))^k with k=7.

formula: G.f.: 1/Q(0), where Q(k)=1 + x*(1+x) - x*(k+1)/(1-x*(k+1)/Q(k+1)); (continued fraction). - _Sergei N. Gladkovskii_, Apr 19 2013
Conjecture D-finite with recurrence a(n) = (n-1)*a(n-1) + (n-1)*a(n-2) + (n-1)*a(n-3) + a(n-4). - _R. J. Mathar_, Jul 26 2022
G.f.: Sum_{k>=0} k! * x^k * ( (1-x)/(1-x^3) )^(k+1). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Feb 20 2024
A177258.name: Number of derangements of {1,2,...,n} having no adjacent transpositions.

formula: Conjecture: D-finite with recurrence a(n) = (n-1)*a(n-1) + (n-1)*a(n-2) + a(n-3) + (n-1)*a(n-4) + 2*a(n-6). - _R. J. Mathar_, Jul 26 2022
G.f.: Sum_{k>=0} k! * x^k / (1+x+x^3)^(k+1). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Feb 22 2024
A177259.name: Number of derangements of {1,2,...,n} having no adjacent 3-cycles (an adjacent 3-cycle is a cycle of the form (i,i+1,i+2)).

formula: Conjecture: D-finite with recurrence a(n) = (n-1)*a(n-1) + (n-1)*a(n-2) + 2*a(n-4) + (n-1)*a(n-5) + 3*a(n-8). - _R. J. Mathar_, Jul 26 2022
G.f.: Sum_{k>=0} k! * x^k / (1+x+x^4)^(k+1). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Feb 22 2024
A177260.name: Number of derangements of {1,2,...,n} having no adjacent 4-cycles (an adjacent 4-cycle is a cycle of the form (i,i+1,i+2,i+3)).

formula: a(n) ~ sqrt((1+r)*(1-r+r^2)*(1-5*r^3)) / (4*sqrt(Pi)*n^(3/2)*r^(n+1)), where r = 0.2587353940253970315668... is the root of the equation (1+r^3)^2 = 4*r. - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Mar 21 2014
a(0) = a(1) = a(2) = 1; a(n) = a(n-3) + Sum_{k=0..n-1} a(k) * a(n-k-1). - _Ilya Gutkovskiy_, Mar 06 2026
A178520.name: Number of ordered trees with n edges and with no vertex of outdegree 2 that have two leaves as their two children.

A179210.name: a(n) is the smallest prime q such that (r-q)/(q-p) = n, where p<q<r are consecutive primes (or 0 if no such prime exists).

formula: After initial term, equals the logarithmic derivative of A156360.
A179504.name: a(n) = sigma(2n,n) for n>0 with a(0)=1.

1/Pi = sqrt(7) Sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n a(n) (11895n + 1286)/22^(3n+3). [Cooper, equation (41)] - _Jason Kimberley_, Nov 06 2012
G.f. A(x) satisfies 1/(1+4*x)^2 * A( x/(1+4*x)^3 ) = 1/(1+2*x)^2 * A( x^2/(1+2*x)^3 ) [see Cooper, Guillera, Straub, Zudilin]. - _Joerg Arndt_, Apr 08 2016
Conjecture D-finite with recurrence: n^3*a(n) - (2*n-1)*(13*n^2-13*n+4)*a(n-1) - 3*(n-1)*(3*n-4)*(3*n-2)*a(n-2) = 0. - _R. J. Mathar_, May 15 2016
The conjectured D-finite recurrence can be proved by Zeilberger's algorithm.
a(n) = Sum_{0 <= j, k <= n} binomial(n, k)^2 * binomial(n, j)^2 * binomial(k+j, n) = Sum_{k = 0..n} binomial(n, k)^2 * A108625(n, k). - _Peter Bala_, Jul 08 2024
a(n) = Sum_{k = 0..n} (-1)^(n-k)*binomial(n+k, k)^3*binomial(3*n+1, n-k). Cf A245086.
a(n) = Sum_{k = 0..n} (-1)^(n+k)*binomial(n, k)*A143007(n, k) (verified using the MulZeil procedure in Doron Zeilberger's MultiZeilberger package). (End)
sqrt(A(x)) = 1 + 2*x + 22*x^2 + 336*x^3 + ... is the g.f. of A279619. - _Peter Bala_, Aug 03 2026
A183204.name: Central terms of triangle A181544.

formula: G.f. A(x) satisfies A(x) = sqrt( 1 + 4*x*A(x)^2 + 12*x^2*A(x)^4 ). - _Paul D. Hanna_, Dec 14 2024
A185020.name: a(n) = A000108(n)*A002605(n+1), where A000108 are the Catalan numbers.

A200312.name: a(n) = A000108(n)*A006130(n), where A000108 is the Catalan numbers and A006130(n) = A006130(n-1) + 3*A006130(n-2).

formula: a(n) = Catalan(n) - Catalan(n-1) + Catalan(n-2). - _Andrei Asinowski_, Dec 16 2015
G.f.: (1 + x + x^2*C(x)^3)*x*C(x) - x where C(x) is the g.f. of A000108. - _Philippe Deléham_, Feb 04 2014
Mathar's conjecture can be verified by expressing a in terms of factorials and simplifying.
A220902.name: a(n) = Catalan(n) - A000245(n-2).

formula: Conjecture: D-finite with recurrence 3*(n+2)*(n-4)*a(n) -(17*n^2-58*n+75)*a(n-1) -3*(n^2-8*n+18)*a(n-2) +(n-3)*(n-5)*a(n-3) = 0. - _Pedro Ferreira Pereira_, Nov 08 2026
Conjecture: a(n) ~ (3 - sqrt(2)) * (1 + sqrt(2))^(2*n-1) / (sqrt(Pi) * 2^(5/4) * n^(3/2)). - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Nov 10 2026
A224292.name: Number of permutations of length n avoiding 1234 and containing exactly 1 occurrence of 1243.

A224748.name: Given n-th prime p, a(n) = number of primes of the form p + q - 1 where q is any prime < p.

A224908.name: Given n-th prime p, a(n)=number of primes of the form p+q+1 where q is any prime < p.

A226302.name: a(n) = P_n(-1), where P_n(x) is a certain polynomial arising in the enumeration of tatami mat coverings.

formula: a(n) = [x^n] I*HeunG(8/5,0,-1/4,1/4,3/2,1/2,16*x)/sqrt(16*x-1) where [x^n] f(x) is the coefficient of x^n in f(x) and HeunG is the Heun general function. (End)
A228329.name: a(n) = Sum_{k=0..n} (k+1)^2*T(n,k)^2 where T(n,k) is the Catalan triangle A039598.

A229019.name: Minimal position at which the sequence defined in the same way as A159559 but with initial term prime(n) merges with A159559; a(n)=0 if there is no such position.

A230219.name: Number of ways to write 2*n + 1 = p + q + r with p <= q such that p, q, r are primes in A230217 and p + q + 9 is also prime.

A234344.name: a(n) = |{0 < k < n: 2^{phi(k)/2} + 3^{phi(n-k)/2} is prime}|, where phi(.) is Euler's totient function.

A234347.name: a(n) = |{0 < k < n: 3^k + 3^{phi(n-k)/2} - 1 is prime}|, where phi(.) is Euler's totient function.

formula: E.g.f.: 1 + Series_Reversion( Integral 1/((2+x)*(1+x+x^2)) dx ). - _Paul D. Hanna_, Jun 16 2015
A258969.name: E.g.f.: A'(x) = 1 + A(x)^3, with A(0)=1.

formula: The g.f. A(x) = Sum_{n>=0} a(n)*x^n satisfies:
a(n) = Sum_{d divides n} (binomial(2*n/d, d-1) + (-1)^(n/d+1) * binomial(n/d, 2*d-1)) for n >= 1.
Hence, a(p) = p + 1 for primes p > 3 and a(2^n) = 1 for n > 0 as conjectured above. (End)
A260147.name: G.f. A(x) = Sum_{n=-oo..+oo} x^n * (1 + x^n)^(2*n).

A261958.name: Start with a single square for n=0; for the odd n-th generation add a square at each expandable vertex of the squares of the (n-1)-th generation (this is the "vertex to vertex" version); for the even n-th generation use the "side to vertex" version; a(n) is the number of squares added in the n-th generation.

formula: Conjectures confirmed since the g.f. satisfies the differential equations corresponding to these recurrences. - _Robert Israel_, Apr 26 2017
A263986.name: Difference between Catalan numbers and Fibonacci numbers: a(n) = C(n) - F(n).

formula: Conjecture D-finite with recurrence (n+1)*a(n) +2*(-1)*a(n-1) +2*(-2*n+3)*a(n-2) +2*(n-6)*a(n-4) +6*(1)*a(n-5) -2*a(n-6) +(n-9)*a(n-8)=0. - _R. J. Mathar_, Jul 22 2022
a(n) ~ sqrt(2*r*(2-3*r)) * (25 + 18*r + 13*r^2) * (1 + r + r^2)^n / (22*sqrt(Pi*n)), where r = A192918. - _Vaclav Kotesovec_, Mar 08 2023
A273905.name: Number of symmetric bargraphs having semiperimeter n (n>=2).

formula: Conjecture: -3*A122858(n) - A229616(n) + 4*a(n) = 0 for all n. - _Thomas Baruchel_, Jun 23 2018
a(n) = 3*sigma(n) - 27*sigma(n/3) = 3 * Sum_{d | n} A061347(d)*d, with the convention that sigma(n/3) = 0 if 3 does not divide n. - _Peter Bala_, Sep 17 2026
b(n) = a(n)/3 is multiplicative with b(3^e) = 4 - 3^(e+1), and b(p^e) = (p^(e+1) - 1)/(p-1) for p != 3.
A282031.name: Coefficients in q-expansion of (9*E_2(q^3) - E_2(q))/8.

A283991.name: a(1) = 0 and for n > 1, a(n) = 1 if Stern polynomial B(n,x) is irreducible, 0 otherwise.

A285195.name: G.f.: 2C(x)/(3-sqrt(1-4xC(x))) where C = g.f. for A000108.

formula: a(n) = A285349(n) - A138518(n) for n>0 (conjectured). - _Thomas Baruchel_, May 14 2018
A285348.name: Expansion of r(q^2) / r(q)^2 in powers of q where r() is the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction.

formula: a(n) = A138518(n) + A285348(n) for n>0 (conjectured). - _Thomas Baruchel_, May 14 2018
A285349.name: Expansion of r(q)^2 / r(q^2) in powers of q where r() is the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction.

formula: F(n) is the n-th Fibonacci number,
T(n) is the n-th triangular number,
a(n) = F(n+1)^2 - T(n-1) - T(F(n-1)) - [n>=4]*U(n) where [] is the Iverson bracket, and U(n) = F(n-1)*F(n-3) + F(n+1)*(2*F(n-4)-1) + 5 - 8*(n mod 2).
Derived from the conjectured order-7 linear recurrence above, for n > 0,
where phi denotes the golden ratio and lim_{n->oo} a(n+1)/a(n) = phi^2.
See the link "Unions and Minkowski sums" for the proof of the formula above. - _Andrei Zabolotskii_, Jul 19 2026
A296516.name: a(n) is the number of terms in expanded form of bivariate polynomial Q_n, where (P_n, Q_n) is defined by: P_0 = x, Q_0 = y, P_(n+1) = P_n + Q_n, Q_(n+1) = P_n * Q_n.

A303539.name: Number of ordered pairs (k, m) with 0 <= k <= m such that n - binomial(2*k,k) - binomial(2*m,m) can be written as the sum of two squares.

A308215.name: a(n) is the multiplicative inverse of A001844(n+1) modulo A001844(n); where A001844 is the sequence of centered square numbers.

A308217.name: a(n) is the multiplicative inverse of A001844(n) modulo A001844(n+1); where A001844 is the sequence of centered square numbers.

formula: E.g.f.: (1/2)*exp(x)*(106 + 858*x + 429*x^2). - conjectured by _Stefano Spezia_, Dec 07 2018 after the conjectures of _Colin Barker_
A322043.name: Numbers k such that the coefficient of x^k in the expansion of Product_{m >= 1} (1-x^m)^15 is zero.

formula: a(n) = (97/144)n^3 - (5/6)n^2 + [44/48, 47/48]n + [0, 13, 8, -45, 40, -19, 0, -5, 8, -27, 40, -37]/72. The value of the first bracket depends on whether n is even or odd. The value of the second bracket depends on whether (n mod 12) is 0, 1, 2, ..., 11.
A322599.name: a(n) is the number of unlabeled rank-3 graded lattices with 4 coatoms and n atoms.

formula: The value of the first bracket depends on whether n is even or odd. The value of the second bracket depends on whether (n mod 60) is 0, 1, 2, ..., 59.
A322600.name: a(n) is the number of unlabeled rank-3 graded lattices with 5 coatoms and n atoms.

A327463.name: a(1) = 1; thereafter, a(n) is the reversal of the next prime after a(n - 1) in base 6 if n is prime, and the reversal of the next composite after a(n - 1) in base 6 if n is composite.

formula: For n > 0, a(n) = 1 (mod 3) iff n = A191107(k) for some k >= 1 (conjecture).
For n > 0, a(n) = 2 (mod 3) iff n = A186776(k) for some k >= 2 where A186776 is the Stanley sequence S(0,2) (conjecture).
A338632.name: G.f. A(x) satisfies: 1 = A(x) - x/(A(x) - 3*x/(A(x) - 5*x/(A(x) - 7*x/(A(x) - 9*x/(A(x) - ...))))), a continued fraction relation.

formula: For n > 0, a(n) = 1 (mod 3) iff n = A191107(k) for some k >= 1 (conjecture).
For n > 0, a(n) = 2 (mod 3) iff n = A186776(k) for some k >= 2 where A186776 is the Stanley sequence S(0,2) (conjecture).
A338636.name: G.f. A(x) satisfies: 1 = A(x) - x/(A(x) - 3^2*x/(A(x) - 5^2*x/(A(x) - 7^2*x/(A(x) - 9^2*x/(A(x) - ...))))), a continued fraction relation.

formula: G.f. A(x) satisfies: A(x) = 1 / (1 - x) + x^5 * A(x)^2.
Conjecture D-finite with recurrence (n+5)*a(n) +2*(-n-4)*a(n-1) +(n+3)*a(n-2) +2*(-2*n+5)*a(n-5) +4*(n-3)*a(n-6)=0. - _R. J. Mathar_, Feb 17 2022
a(n) = Sum_{k=0..floor(n/5)} binomial(n-4*k,k) * Catalan(k). - _Seiichi Manyama_, Jan 22 2023
A346074.name: a(n) = 1 + Sum_{k=0..n-5} a(k) * a(n-k-5).

A359984.name: Number of non-crossing antichain covers of {1,...,n} without singletons.

formula: a(n) = [A000203(n) >= 2*n-1], where [ ] is the Iverson bracket.
A378550.name: a(n) = 1 if sigma(n) >= 2*n-1, otherwise 0.

A379464.name: a(n) is the total number of paths starting at (0, 0), ending at (n, 0), consisting of steps (1, 1), (1, 0), (1, -3), and staying on or above y = -2.

formula: G.f. A(x) = Sum_{n>=1} a(n)*x^n satisfies the following formulas.
(1.a) (A(x) + A(-x))/2 = (-2*A(x) + 5*A(x)^2 + 2*x)/3, the even bisection of A(x).
(1.b) (A(x) - A(-x))/2 = (5*A(x) - 5*A(x)^2 - 2*x)/3, the odd bisection of A(x).
(2.a) (A(x)^2 + A(-x)^2)/2 = (A(x) + A(-x))/2, the even bisection of A(x)^2.
(2.b) (A(x)^2 - A(-x)^2)/2 = (A(x) - A(-x))/5 - 2*x/5, the odd bisection of A(x)^2.
(5.b) (A(x) - A(-x))/2 = Series_Reversion( x - 5*x*C(x^2) ) where C(x) = (1 - sqrt(1 - 4*x))/2 is a g.f. of the Catalan numbers (A000108).
A392211.name: G.f. satisfies A(x) = (1 - sqrt(1 + 4*A(-x) - 4*A(-x)^2))/2.

A397621.name: a(n) is the linear complexity over GF(2) of the binary expansion of n (as computed by the Berlekamp-Massey algorithm).
